dhpak1.5:1.1: “For not by hatred do hatreds cease,”
dhpak1.5:1.2: [28.166] {1.45} this Dhamma teaching was given by the Teacher while he was in residence at Jetavana with reference to a certain barren woman.
dhpak1.5:2.1: It appears that a certain householder’s son, on the death of his father,
dhpak1.5:2.2: did all the farm and household work by himself alone and took care of his mother also.
dhpak1.5:2.3: Now his mother said to him: “Dear son, I will fetch you a young woman to wife.”
dhpak1.5:2.4: – “Dear mother, speak not thus; my sole desire is to care for you so long as you shall live.”
dhpak1.5:2.5: – “Dear son, you alone are doing all the farm and household work, and I am not satisfied to have it so; let me fetch you a young woman to wife.”
dhpak1.5:2.6: He protested time and again, and then held his peace.
dhpak1.5:3.1: The mother left the house, intending to go to a certain family and fetch home the daughter of that family.
dhpak1.5:3.2: Her son asked her: “To what family are you going?” – “To such and such a family.”
dhpak1.5:3.3: He would not let her go to the family she had in mind, but told her of a family he liked better.
dhpak1.5:3.4: So she went to the family he fancied, selected a wife [28.171] for her son,
dhpak1.5:3.5: and having set the day, installed her in her son’s house. The woman turned out to be barren.
dhpak1.5:4.1: Then said the mother to the son: “Son, you had me fetch you a wife you yourself selected.
dhpak1.5:4.2: Now she turns out to be barren. Without children a family {1.46} dies out, and the line is not continued.
dhpak1.5:4.3: Therefore let me fetch you another young woman to wife.”
dhpak1.5:4.4: – “Enough said, dear mother,” replied the son; but the mother repeated her request time and again.
dhpak1.5:4.5: The barren wife heard the talk and thought to herself: “It is certain that sons cannot disobey the words of their mothers and fathers.
dhpak1.5:4.6: Now if she fetches him a wife who is fruitful, they will treat me like a slave.
dhpak1.5:4.7: Suppose I were to fetch him a young woman of my own selection?”
dhpak1.5:5.1: So the barren wife went to a certain family and selected a young woman for him.
dhpak1.5:5.2: But she immediately encountered the opposition of the young woman’s parents, who said to her: “Woman, what say you?”
dhpak1.5:5.3: The barren wife replied: “I am a barren woman, and without children a family dies out.
dhpak1.5:5.4: If your daughter gives birth to a son, she will be mistress of the family and the wealth thereof.
dhpak1.5:5.5: Therefore give your daughter to me for my husband.”
dhpak1.5:5.6: She finally prevailed upon them to grant her request, and taking the young woman with her, installed her in her husband’s house.
dhpak1.5:6.1: Then this thought occurred to her: “If my rival gives birth to a son or a daughter, she alone will be mistress of the household.
dhpak1.5:6.2: I must see to it that she shall not give birth to a child.”
dhpak1.5:6.3: So the barren wife said to her rival:
dhpak1.5:6.4: “As soon as you have conceived a child in your womb, pray let me know.” – “Very well,” replied her rival.
dhpak1.5:6.5: In accordance with her promise, as soon as she had conceived, she told her fellow-wife.
dhpak1.5:7.1: Now the barren wife was accustomed to give her rival a meal of rice-porridge regularly every day with her own hand.
dhpak1.5:7.2: {1.47} So along with the food she gave her a drug to cause abortion. The result was that her rival had a miscarriage.
dhpak1.5:7.3: Again the second time the fruitful wife conceived a child and informed the barren wife.
dhpak1.5:7.4: And again her fellow-wife did as before and brought about a miscarriage.
dhpak1.5:8.1: A Barren Womb The women who lived in the neighborhood asked the fruitful wife: “Is not your rival putting an obstacle in your way?”
dhpak1.5:8.2: When she told them the facts, they said to her: “You foolish woman, why did you do this?
dhpak1.5:8.3: This woman was afraid you would get the upper hand.
dhpak1.5:8.4: So she mixed a preparation to bring about a miscarriage and gave it to you. Do not tell her again.”
dhpak1.5:8.5: Accordingly the third time the fruitful wife [28.172] said nothing to her rival.
dhpak1.5:8.6: But the barren wife, seeing her belly, said to her: “Why did you not tell me that you had conceived a child?”
dhpak1.5:8.7: The fruitful wife said: “It was you who brought me here, and twice you have caused me to suffer a miscarriage; why should I tell you?”
dhpak1.5:8.8: – “Now I am lost,” thought the barren wife.
dhpak1.5:9.1: From that time on she watched to catch her rival off her guard.
dhpak1.5:9.2: When the baby in the womb was fully matured, she took advantage of an opportunity, mixed a drug, and gave it to her.
dhpak1.5:9.3: But because the baby in her womb was fully mature, an abortion was out of the question,
dhpak1.5:9.4: and the result was that the child lodged across the neck of the womb.
dhpak1.5:9.5: Immediately the mother suffered acute pains and feared that her hour had come.
dhpak1.5:10.1: “You have killed me!” she cried. “It was you alone that brought me here;
dhpak1.5:10.2: it was you alone that killed my three children. Now I also am going to die.
dhpak1.5:10.3: When I have passed out of this existence, may I be reborn as a Yakkhinī able to devour your children.”
dhpak1.5:10.4: And having made this aspiration, she died, {1.48} and was reborn in that very house as a cat.
dhpak1.5:11.1: The husband seized the barren wife, and saying to her:
dhpak1.5:11.2: “It was you who destroyed my family,” beat her soundly with elbows, knees, and otherwise.
dhpak1.5:11.3: As the result of the beating she received, she sickened and died, and was reborn in that very house as a hen.
dhpak1.5:12.1: So the fruitful wife was reborn as a
dhpak1.5:12.3: and the barren wife was reborn as a
dhpak1.5:13.1: The hen laid eggs, and the cat came and ate them. This happened three times.
dhpak1.5:13.2: Said the hen: “Three times have you eaten my eggs, and now you are seeking an opportunity to eat me too.
dhpak1.5:13.3: When I have passed out of this existence, may I be able to eat you and your offspring.”
dhpak1.5:13.4: And having made this aspiration, she passed out of that existence, and was reborn as a leopardess. The cat was reborn as a doe.
dhpak1.5:14.1: So the barren wife, at the end of her existence as a hen, was reborn as a leopardess;
dhpak1.5:14.2: and the fruitful wife, at the end of her existence as a cat, was reborn as a doe.
dhpak1.5:15.1: Thrice the doe brought forth young, and thrice the leopardess went and devoured the doe’s offspring.
dhpak1.5:15.2: When the doe came to die, she said: “Thrice this beast has devoured my offspring, and now she purposes to devour me too.
dhpak1.5:15.3: When I have passed out of this existence, may I be able to devour her and her offspring.”
dhpak1.5:15.4: And having made this aspiration, she was reborn as a Yakkhinī.
dhpak1.5:15.5: When the leopardess passed out of that existence, she was reborn at Sāvatthī as a young woman of station.
dhpak1.5:16.1: So the fruitful wife, at the end of her existence as a doe, was reborn as a Yakkhinī;
dhpak1.5:16.2: and the barren wife, at the end of her existence as a [28.173] leopardess,
dhpak1.5:16.3: was reborn at Sāvatthī as a young woman of station.
dhpak1.5:17.1: When the latter grew up, she was married and went to live with her husband’s family in a little settlement near the gate of the city.
dhpak1.5:17.2: After a time she gave birth to a son.
dhpak1.5:17.3: The Yakkhinī disguised herself as a dear friend of the young woman and went to see her.
dhpak1.5:17.4: “Where is my friend?” said the Yakkhinī. “In the inner room; she has just given birth to a child.”
dhpak1.5:17.5: – “Did she give birth to a son or a daughter? I should like to see her.” So saying, the Yakkhinī went in.
dhpak1.5:17.6: While pretending to be looking at the child, she seized him, devoured him, and then went out.
dhpak1.5:18.1: Again a second time she devoured a child of the young wife in the same way.
dhpak1.5:18.2: The third time the young wife was great with child she addressed her husband: “Husband, in this place a Yakkhinī has devoured two sons of mine and escaped.
dhpak1.5:18.3: {1.49} This time I intend to go to the house of my parents to give birth to my child.”
dhpak1.5:18.4: Now at this time that Yakkhinī was away doing her turn at drawing water.
dhpak1.5:19.1: For Vessavaṇa’s Yakkhinīs take their turn at drawing water from Lake Anotatta, passing it along from the source.
dhpak1.5:19.2: At the expiration of four or five months they are released;
dhpak1.5:20.1: The moment the Yakkhinī was released from her turn at drawing water she went quickly to the young wife’s house and enquired:
dhpak1.5:20.2: “Where is my friend?” – “Where you will not see her.
dhpak1.5:20.3: There is a Yakkhinī that devours every child she bears in this house, and therefore, she has gone to the house of her parents.”
dhpak1.5:20.4: – “She may go wherever she likes, but she will not escape from me.”
dhpak1.5:20.5: Spurred on by an impulse of hatred, the Yakkhinī dashed towards the city.
dhpak1.5:21.1: On the day appointed for the naming of the child the mother bathed him, gave him a name, and then said to her husband:
dhpak1.5:21.2: “Husband, now we will go back to our own home.”
dhpak1.5:21.3: Accordingly she took the boy in her arms and set out with her husband along the path leading through the grounds of the monastery.
dhpak1.5:21.4: When they reached the monastery pool, the young wife gave the boy to her husband and bathed in the pool.
dhpak1.5:21.5: When she had finished her bath, her husband bathed in the pool.
dhpak1.5:21.6: While the husband was bathing, the wife remained near, giving suck to her child.
dhpak1.5:22.1: Just then the Yakkhinī drew near. The young wife saw her coming and recognized her.
dhpak1.5:22.2: Immediately she screamed with a loud voice: “Husband! Husband! Come quickly! Come quickly! Here is that Yakkhinī!”
dhpak1.5:22.3: Not daring to wait until her husband came, {1.50} she turned and dashed into the monastery.
dhpak1.5:23.1: Now at this time the Teacher was teaching the Dhamma in the midst [28.174] of the assembly.
dhpak1.5:23.2: The young wife laid her boy at the feet of the Realised One and said: “I give you this child; spare the life of my son.”
dhpak1.5:23.3: The Deva Sumana, who resided in the embattled chamber over the gate, prevented the Yakkhinī from entering.
dhpak1.5:23.4: The Teacher addressed the Elder Ānanda, saying: “Go, Ānanda, summon that Yakkhinī within.”
dhpak1.5:23.5: The elder summoned her within. The young wife said: “Here she comes, venerable Sir.”
dhpak1.5:23.6: Said the Teacher: “Let her come; make no noise.”
dhpak1.5:24.1: When the Yakkhinī came and stood before him, the Teacher said: “Why have you so done?
dhpak1.5:24.2: Had you not come face to face with a Buddha like me, you would have cherished hatred towards each other for an aeon,
dhpak1.5:24.3: like the snake and the mongoose, who trembled and quaked with enmity, like the crows and the owls.
dhpak1.5:24.4: Why do you return hatred for hatred? Hatred is quenched by non-hatred, not by hatred.”
dhpak1.5:24.5: And when he had thus spoken, he pronounced the following verse:
dhpak1.5:25.1: 5. Na hi verena verāni sammantīdha kudācanaṁ,
dhpak1.5:25.2: averena ca sammanti, esa dhammo sanantano.
dhpak1.5:26.1: For not by hatred do hatreds cease at any time in this place,
dhpak1.5:26.2: they only cease with non-hatred, this truth is surely eternal. {1.51}
dhpak1.5:27.1: At the conclusion of the verse the Yakkhinī was established in Stream-entry.
dhpak1.5:27.2: And the Dhamma teaching was of benefit to the assembly.
dhpak1.5:28.1: Not by Hatred The Teacher said to the woman: “Give your child to this Yakkhinī.”
dhpak1.5:28.2: – “I am afraid to, venerable Sir.” – “Fear not.
dhpak1.5:28.3: You have no reason to be alarmed because of her.” The young wife gave her child to the Yakkhinī.
dhpak1.5:28.4: The Yakkhinī kissed and caressed him, gave him back again to his mother, and began to weep.
dhpak1.5:28.5: The Teacher asked her: “Why do you weep?”
dhpak1.5:28.6: – “Venerable Sir, in the past I have managed somehow or other to get a living, but I have never had enough to eat.
dhpak1.5:28.7: Now how am I to live?” Then the Teacher comforted her, saying: “Do not worry.” And turning to the mother, he said:
dhpak1.5:28.8: {1.52} “Take this Yakkhinī home with you, let her live in your own house, and feed her with the choicest rice-porridge.”
dhpak1.5:29.1: So the young wife took the Yakkhinī home with her, lodged her on the central rafter of the hut, and fed her with the choicest rice-porridge.
dhpak1.5:29.2: Now when the rice was threshed and the flail was raised, she feared that it would strike her head.
dhpak1.5:29.3: So she said to her friend: “I shall not be able to live here any longer; lodge me elsewhere.”
dhpak1.5:29.4: She was lodged successively in the grinding-hut, the water-pot, the bake-house, the storeroom for nimbs, the dust-heap, and the village gate.
dhpak1.5:29.5: But she refused [28.175] to live in any of these places, saying:
dhpak1.5:29.6: “Here the flail rises as if it would split my head in two;
dhpak1.5:29.7: here boys empty out slops; here dogs lie down; here boys attend to nature’s needs;
dhpak1.5:29.8: here they throw away sweepings; here village boys practice fortune-telling.”
dhpak1.5:29.9: So they lodged her in a quiet place by herself outside of the village, and there they brought her the choicest rice-porridge.
dhpak1.5:30.1: The Yakkhinī said to her friend: “This year there will be abundance of rain;
dhpak1.5:30.2: therefore plant your crops in a dry place.
dhpak1.5:30.3: This year there will be a drought; therefore plant your crops in a moist place.”
dhpak1.5:30.4: Other people’s crops were destroyed either by excessive moisture or by drought, but the crops of the young wife flourished above measure.
dhpak1.5:31.1: People asked the young wife: “Woman, your crops are destroyed neither by excessive moisture nor by drought.
dhpak1.5:31.2: When you plant your crops, you seem to know in advance whether the season will be wet or dry.
dhpak1.5:31.3: How is this?” The young wife replied:
dhpak1.5:31.4: “I have a friend, a Yakkhinī, {1.53} who tells me whether the season will be wet or dry;
dhpak1.5:31.5: and I plant my crops according to her directions on high or low ground. Don’t you see?
dhpak1.5:31.6: Every day the choicest rice-porridge and other kinds of food are carried out of our house; to her are they carried.
dhpak1.5:31.7: Do you also carry the choicest rice-porridge and other kinds of food to her, and she will look after your crops also.”
dhpak1.5:32.1: Straightaway all the residents of the city rendered honor to her.
dhpak1.5:32.2: On her part, from that time forth, she looked after the crops of all. And she received abundant gifts and a large retinue.
dhpak1.5:32.3: Subsequently she established the eight ticket-foods, which are kept up even to this present day.
